concerns.concern: The headline ~5.5% softening rests on only seven temperature points. It is measured against a single 200 K local maximum, so the size of the effect depends on which paramagnetic point is chosen; relative to 300 K the drop is only ~2–3%.
concerns.quote: The 'PM reference' is a single local maximum at 200 K.

concerns.concern: The 300 K velocity in Fig. 4 (~1865 m/s) differs by ~4% from the room-temperature velocity at the same q in Fig. 3 (~1945 m/s). This systematic scatter is comparable to the claimed magnetic effect, and the paper does not say whether the same flake and setup were used.
concerns.quote: This ~4% run-to-run (or sample-to-sample) discrepancy at nominally identical conditions is comparable to the 5.5% magnetic effect being claimed.

concerns.concern: There are no data between 200 K and 150 K, so the onset of the drop cannot be tied to T_N. It might begin well above T_N because of short-range correlations.
concerns.quote: There are no data between 200 and 150 K, so the drop cannot be localized to T_N (~155 K).

concerns.concern: The DFT/FEM model predicts only a 0.54% shift, about ten times smaller than measured, yet the abstract claims theory 'reproduces' the shift. The paper attributes the gap to finite-temperature effects and the NM proxy without giving evidence for either.
concerns.quote: The FEM model with DFT tensors gives a 0.54% frequency decrease (4.603 → 4.578 GHz), roughly ten times smaller than the measured ~5.5%.

concerns.concern: Calling the absolute room-temperature agreement 'close' overstates it. The simulated frequency is ~10% too high (4.6 vs 4.2 GHz) and the simulated velocities are well above the measured ones, both discrepancies being larger than the effect of interest.
concerns.quote: Calling 4.6 vs 4.2 GHz 'close agreement' ... is therefore an overstatement.

concerns.concern: There is no temperature-dependent control on the bare SiO2/Si substrate. Anomalous SiO2 elasticity and thermal-contraction strain or delamination could produce percent-level velocity changes unrelated to magnetism. The FEM uses fixed substrate constants, and no non-magnetic reference flake was measured.
concerns.quote: The paper shows bare-substrate spectra only at RT (Supplementary Fig. 5), so these contributions are not excluded.

concerns.concern: BMS laser heating is not characterized. mW-level power on an absorbing flake sitting on poorly conducting SiO2 could raise the local temperature by tens of kelvin, shifting or smearing the apparent anomaly relative to T_N.
concerns.quote: this can raise the local temperature by tens of kelvin.

concerns.concern: The claim that the data imply a reduction of shear and out-of-plane constants conflicts with the DFT, which leaves c44 unchanged between NM and AFM. The experiment would need a >10% drop in c44, and even more once the substrate's share of the wave energy is accounted for.
concerns.quote: The experiment would therefore require a large (>10%) magnetically induced reduction of c44 that the DFT does not predict at all.

concerns.concern: The low-temperature points scatter non-monotonically, with error bars up to ±25 m/s. This makes the claimed saturation and step shape hard to establish.
concerns.quote: Error bars reach ±25 m/s, and the low-T points are non-monotonic (1818 → 1837 → 1832 → 1805).

concerns.concern: The ~3% stiffening between 300 K and 200 K is unusually large for ordinary anharmonicity, and the paper does not explain it.
concerns.quote: The 3% stiffening between 300 and 200 K over just 100 K is itself unusually large for ordinary anharmonicity, and is not explained.

concerns.concern: The data come from a single flake without repeated thermal cycles, so the reproducibility of the anomaly is not established.
concerns.quote: plus repeated cooling/heating cycles and at least one additional flake.

concerns.concern: Using a spin-unpolarized non-magnetic state as a proxy for the paramagnetic phase quenches the robust Ni2+ local moment. The NM–AFM difference therefore mixes moment formation with ordering and is not a clean estimate of the order-induced elastic change.
concerns.quote: The NM–AFM difference therefore mixes moment formation with magnetic ordering.

concerns.concern: The phenomenological renormalization uses the uniform susceptibility. For an antiferromagnet that quantity is smooth at T_N and nonzero above it, so the formula would predict softening in the PM phase and no step at T_N.
concerns.quote: For an antiferromagnet the uniform χ is finite and smooth at T_N, and it is nonzero above T_N

concerns.concern: The DFT uses plain PBE-D3 without a Hubbard U and does not mention spin–orbit coupling. Standard practice for NiPS3 is DFT+U, and the AFM/NM elastic differences are sensitive to this choice.
concerns.quote: The functional is plain PBE-D3 with no Hubbard U, and no spin–orbit coupling is mentioned.

concerns.concern: The stated supercell multiplicity (1×4×2) does not match the quoted lattice dimensions, which correspond to roughly 2×2×2. One of the two is misreported, which affects whether the magnetic cell can be reproduced.
concerns.quote: Either the multiplicity or the lattice dimensions are misreported, which matters for reproducing the magnetic cell.

concerns.concern: The magnetoelastic argument is circular. The measured 5.5% is presented as a consequence of the formula even though no coupling constants are estimated.
concerns.quote: presents the measured number as a consequence of the formula, although no coupling constants are estimated.

concerns.concern: The magnetoelastic energy mixes coupling forms. It is written as a single-ion form in spin components, while B is described as a strain derivative of exchange, which would couple to S_i·S_j.
concerns.quote: Yet B_αβ is described as the strain derivative of the exchange J_ij, which would instead couple to S_i·S_j

concerns.concern: The FEM model is underspecified: densities, substrate constants, Si orientation, tensor rotation, domain depth and mesh are not given. Numerical convergence of the small 25 MHz AFM–NM difference is not demonstrated.
concerns.quote: numerical convergence with respect to mesh and domain depth also needs to be demonstrated.

concerns.concern: It is unclear why the FEM applies 3D Floquet periodic conditions along both x and y with a single wavevector k.
concerns.quote: It is also unclear why 3D Floquet conditions are applied along both x and y with a single k.

concerns.concern: Key BMS acquisition parameters are not reported, so the measurement cannot be assessed or reproduced. Missing items include laser power, spot size, NA, accumulation time, temperature stabilization, free spectral range and resolution.
concerns.quote: laser power on the sample, spot size and objective NA

concerns.concern: Zigzag AFM order forms three 120°-rotated domains, so the measured response likely averages over domains. Interpreting the shift relative to the spin-chain direction (q ∥ b) is therefore not justified.
concerns.quote: the measured response therefore likely averages over domains

concerns.concern: Identifying crystal axes from 60° cleavage edges by optical microscopy is unreliable in nearly hexagonal NiPS3. The a-axis cannot be distinguished from other zigzag directions by edge morphology alone.
concerns.quote: the a-axis cannot be distinguished from the other two zigzag directions by edge morphology alone.

concerns.concern: The surface-ripple selection rule is misstated. Scattering requires a displacement component normal to the surface, not merely one perpendicular to propagation, which weakens the argument that only the Rayleigh mode should appear.
concerns.quote: Merely being perpendicular to the propagation direction is not enough

concerns.concern: Because NiPS3 absorbs at 532 nm, elasto-optic scattering from the film volume may also contribute to the Brillouin signal. The paper does not consider this.
concerns.quote: NiPS3 absorbs at 532 nm, so elasto-optic scattering from the film volume may also contribute.

concerns.concern: The conclusion that optical phonons are insensitive may reflect limited Raman resolution and SNR rather than physics. Prior magnetic signatures, such as the mode splitting, are not reproduced, and the Methods wrongly claims that low laser power improves SNR.
concerns.quote: The absence of signatures may therefore reflect limited spectral resolution or SNR.

concerns.concern: The 'giant' and 'two-dimensional' framing is overstated for a ~220 nm, bulk-like flake of several hundred layers. Percent-level elastic anomalies are well known in bulk magnets, and the cited spin–phonon constants concern optical phonons rather than elastic constants.
concerns.quote: The 'giant' and 'rarely reported in 2D magnets' language is not supported by the data presented.

concerns.concern: Calling c66 the most notable change is wrong. c12 changes more, both absolutely and relatively, and the c66 change simply follows from it; neither constant affects the Rayleigh wave along b.
concerns.quote: c12 changes by −11.2 GPa (−22%), which is larger both absolutely and relatively than c66 (+8.0 GPa, +17%).

concerns.concern: The emphasized sign reversal of c35 is below the typical numerical uncertainty of finite-difference DFT elastic constants. No uncertainty estimate for the elastic constants is given.
concerns.quote: is below the typical numerical uncertainty of finite-difference DFT elastic constants at strain 0.015.
